subject: Biotechnology
title: Hybridoma Technology
description: Learn Hybridoma Technology in one minute.

hook.text: B cells make antibodies but die quickly in culture — cancer cells are immortal but make no useful antibodies.

buildup.text: Köhler and Milstein fused them — creating hybridomas that are both immortal and antibody-producing.

discovery.text: HAT selection medium kills unfused cells — only the hybrid survives, producing unlimited monoclonal antibodies.

twist.text: The inventors did not patent it — they shared the technology freely. It won them the 1984 Nobel Prize.

climax.text: Hybridoma technology launched a multibillion-dollar industry — from research reagents to life-saving drugs.

punchline.text: Fuse a B cell with a cancer cell — get an immortal antibody factory.

quiz.question: What is a hybridoma?
options: A type of virus used to deliver antibodies
A fusion of an antibody-producing B cell and an immortal cancer cell
A genetically modified bacterium that secretes antibodies

details.summary: Hybridoma technology fuses antibody-producing B cells with immortal myeloma cells to create cell lines that produce unlimited quantities of a single specific antibody. Invented in 1975, it earned Kohler and Milstein the Nobel Prize and launched the monoclonal antibody industry.
details.whyItMatters: Hybridoma technology made monoclonal antibodies practical for the first time. Although newer methods like phage display exist, hybridomas remain widely used in research and were the foundation for a multi-hundred-billion-dollar therapeutic antibody
takeaways: Hybridomas fuse B cells with myeloma cells to create antibody factories
The technology earned the 1984 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
It enabled the entire monoclonal antibody therapeutics industry

faq.question: How does hybridoma technology work step by step?
faq.answer: An animal is immunized with the target antigen. Antibody-producing B cells from its spleen are fused with immortal myeloma cells using PEG or electrofusion. Survivor cells are selected in HAT medium, then screened for the desired antibody. Positive clones are expanded for production.

faq.question: Why did Kohler and Milstein not patent hybridoma technology?
faq.answer: They published without patenting because MRC guidelines at the time discouraged it. The UK government later estimated this cost billions in lost revenue. The oversight led to changes in academic patenting policies and is frequently cited as a lesson in intellectual property strategy.
